prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1332; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured after a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane road. The insured states the other vehicle drifted into their lane as they moved over, and the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Recorded statements from two independent witnesses and the other driver all describe the collision the same way as the insured. Police confirm the claimant was seated in the insured vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: Photos of the vehicle show damage along the right side that matches the described impact. A few older scratches are visible in the same area, and they may predate this loss, so they will be separated during estimating.

Entry 4: Coverage history reviewed. Nothing indicates the damage occurred before the policy period began, and the vehicle was insured continuously through the loss date.

Entry 5: Claimant reports knee pain from the collision and is represented by counsel. Claimant has given the same account of events in every conversation so far. No prior injury to the knee is known from the records obtained, though it is not yet clear whether the injury resulted from this crash.

Entry 6: Medical records received show treatment that followed a typical course, with visits tapering off as the claimant's condition improved. Causation remains under review pending the treating provider's written opinion.

Entry 7: File remains open for the medical causation review and receipt of the final bills. Liability appears clear based on the consistent statements and physical evidence, and the damage estimate is being finalized.
